reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports graphene's high strength and its strengthening effect in Cu, Al, and Ni composites, but it does not mention graphene's thermal conductivity, irradiation tolerance, or its behavior in W–Cu systems, leaving most key premises unsupported.
premises: Graphene has ultrahigh in-plane thermal conductivity that can provide efficient heat-transfer channels in a composite.
Graphene has excellent mechanical strength that can help preserve structural integrity of a composite.
Graphene can form percolating networks bridging tungsten and copper domains when aligned at interfaces.
Graphene addition in metal composites (Cu, Al, Ni) leads to significant strength enhancement via metal–graphene interfaces.
